<!-- pr-reviewer: 60a6df15499005746c153c06319fae0cfdefaa4a -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (two small wording notes below, not blocking).

**What looks good**
- Only two new `.mch` data files, the `MACHINES` list entries, test updates and a decision record. No build.rs, scripts, `.github` or dependency changes; no mill file or mill code path is touched, so mill output is unchanged.
- Both files parse and mount: `general.kind` is `lathe`, units `inch`, X/Z only (no Y), flood coolant, tool counts 99 / 8, all as the new `tormach_lathes` suite pins.
- Figures are mutually consistent: 8L spindle 180-5000 with ranges 180-2500 / 350-5000; 15L 180-2500; feed equals rapid (150 / 60 IPM); power 1.1 kW (8L) and 2.24 kW (15L, 3 hp), in kW like the shipped `lathe.mch`. Choices that err conservative (8L X 4.5", 15L top speed at the chuck rating) are recorded in `docs/decisions/611-tormach-lathes.md`.
- Clean-room: numbers cited to Tormach's public manuals (UM10753 3.1, UM10225 1.1); no vendor-CAM material or post text.
- The `tormach_safe_retract` skip (`crates/app/tests/tormach_safe_retract.rs`, +5) is narrow: it only skips `Kind::Lathe`, and the Z0 retract law is a mill-post law (a lathe retracts in X/Z). It does not weaken the check for any mill; the Tormach mills are still asserted byte-identical.

**Local results (merged with fresh upstream/main, clean auto-merge)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| tormach_lathes | 2 passed |
| machine | 32 passed |
| machine_library | 11 passed |
| tormach_machines | 5 passed |
| tormach_safe_retract | 4 passed |
| sinumerik_safe_retract / inverted_probe / axis_direction / machine_edit | 3 / 8 / 12 / 12 passed |
| camcraft-ui `machines_pane` (from crates/ui) | 3 passed |
| clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. The decision record says the 8L's 4.5" X "refuses more, never less". The `-4.5..+4.5` band (both files, `travel`) is the mills' full-stroke-either-way convention, so it actually permits 9" of span, twice the stroke, and differs from the shipped `lathe.mch` (X `0..320`). The record's own "catches a gross over-travel" wording is the accurate one; consider dropping the "refuses more" claim, and whether lathe X wants `0..stroke` (or a diameter reading) as the generic lathe has.
2. Stale wording: `crates/app/src/posting.rs:142`, and the header of `crates/app/tests/tormach_lathes.rs` (lines 3-4, 10), still say "public spec sheets" while the PR body and decision cite the operator manuals. Worth one line of alignment. The 8L's 1.1 kW comes from Tormach's web page, not the manual (the record says so).
3. The safe-retract test could instead assert that lathes do not state a Z0 retract, so a future lathe mistake is still caught; optional.
4. Default post is still Fanuc lathe until #612 (as the PR states); the Hub run is not exercised. I did not run it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: a5756b59bbd1ee4bdbc806df05b18549787a08fb -->
Delta review (merge of main only): since the last reviewed head 60a6df1, the only new commit is the merge of main (a5756b5).

- Resolution is right. `MACHINES` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` keeps #618's two M+ entries first, then the 8L and 15L Slant-PRO lathes. `every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_spec...` in `crates/app/tests/machine.rs` lists the same order.
- Nothing from main was dropped: `git diff upstream/main HEAD --stat` lists only the PR's 7 files (two .mch, posting.rs, machine.rs, tormach_lathes.rs, tormach_safe_retract.rs, the decisions file).

Local results (PR head, merges with main cleanly, CARGO_TARGET_DIR shared):
- `machine` 32/32, `machine_library` 11/11, `posting` 17/17, `tormach_lathes` 2/2, `tormach_machines` 6/6, `tormach_safe_retract` 4/4 pass.
- clippy `-D warnings` on the app lib and those six test targets: clean.
- Note: a full `--tests` build of camcraft-app fails in `lathe_thread_travel` (#686, a main-side error, not this PR), so suites were built individually.

Nothing requested. A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
